problem_statement: The paper frames the problem as ultra-low-latency decision-making for high-frequency trading in global markets, together with portfolio optimization and short-term market prediction. It says the goal is to support real-time trading strategies that can respond to market changes quickly and handle volatility.
problem_statement_quotes:
The ultra-low-latency decision-making process 
and sophisticated predictive technology are the key to staying 
competitive in the rapidly evolving global markets with the 
continuous fading of timeframes in affected markets.

This study introduces a 
quantum inspired model that integrates an encoding of 
quantum data, quantum approximate optimization, and 
quantum neural networks to generate real-time trading 
strategies.

A quantum computing integration into high-frequency trading 
(HFT) presents a novel solution, that addresses one of the 
major issues in global markets: ultra-low-latency decision-
making, multi-level portfolio optimization, and forecasting.
classical_baseline: The paper treats classical algorithms, traditional statistical models, and traditional machine learning procedures as the baseline. It also compares against ARIMA, SVM, DNN, and a quantum-inspired optimization approach in its results section.
classical_baseline_quotes:
Classical 
algorithms are efficient but have limitations in scaling, speed, 
and non-linear market applications.

In contrast to classical statistical models and 
traditional machine learning procedures, the quantum-driven 
system utilizes parallelism to handle large volumes of 
financial data in real-time, which makes the quantum-enabled 
approach serve quicker and more trustworthy trading 
decisions.
classical_difficulty: The paper says classical methods struggle with scaling, speed, and non-linear market applications, and that classical computers struggle to perform optimization, forecasting, and execution at the extremely low latency required for HFT. It also says classical techniques face challenges in scaling to large portfolios and handling noisy signals.
classical_difficulty_quotes:
Classical algorithms are efficient but have limitations in scaling, speed, 
and non-linear market applications.

However, in the real world, as markets become increasingly interconnected 
and trade volumes increase, classical computers struggle to 
perform the optimization, forecasting, and execution of 
workloads with the extremely low latency required for high-
frequency trading [2].

Classical techniques face challenges in scaling to a large 
portfolio of assets, handling noisy signals, and pricing real-
time volatility.
business_stakes: The paper says even slight speed improvements can increase profits in HFT, and that the system is meant to remain competitive in global markets. It also mentions risk-adjusted returns and regulatory compliance as practical concerns.
business_stakes_quotes:
Trades occur in micro seconds, and even the 
slightest improvements in speed can increase profits [1].

The only viable strategies for 
remaining competitive should be their ability to trade quickly 
and remain resilient during volatility, delays, and cyber 
threats.

The regulatory compliance is participated by limiting the 
framework to decision-support and execution optimization layers without 
breaking the rules of exchange fairness, transparency, and 
market abuse.
extraction_notes: Motivation is explicit in abstract and introduction; paper is strongly framed around HFT latency, prediction, and portfolio optimization.
